title: Company-wide policies and process documentation (expanded)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This page centralizes Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard processes for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding and management, travel policy, and internal templates. The goal is to provide a single reference for common cross-functional procedures, approval thresholds, owners, and links to templates.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and contingent workers unless otherwise noted.
- Where a function-specific process exists (e.g., engineering runbooks, security playbooks), this page provides the canonical cross-team policy and links to the detailed operational docs.

Owners & contacts:
- Policy owner: People Ops (primary contact: Aisha Patel).
- Finance owner (procurement & expenses): Finance & Legal (contact: Maya Singh).
- Security & compliance owner (data handling, vendor security reviews): Security & Compliance (contact: Carlos Rivera).
- Escalation path: People Ops -> Finance -> Legal -> Security.

1) Access and Permissions
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access while enabling teams to move quickly.
Key principles:
- Role-based access control (RBAC) is our default. Personal accounts map to roles (engineer, sde-lead, infra-admin, finance, hr-admin, etc.).
- Just-in-time (JIT) elevation is required for high-risk operations (production infra, customer data export).
- All access must be provisioned and revoked via our identity provider (IdP). Manual account changes are not permitted except in documented emergency procedures.
Standard roles and examples:
- viewer: read-only access to dashboards and docs.
- contributor: edit access to code repos and non-prod infra.
- operator: permission to deploy to staging and run playbooks.
- infra-admin: infrastructure-level privileges (limited to named personnel).
- security-admin: audit and incident privileges.
Onboarding/offboarding process:
1. New hires are assigned a baseline role during HR onboarding.
2. Team leads request additional roles via the Access Request Form (link in Templates). Requests must include justification and intended duration if temporary.
3. Access provisioning SLA: 48 hours for standard requests; 4 hours for emergency JIT (requires manager approval).
4. Offboarding: People Ops triggers automated revocation on termination date; teams must confirm return of hardware and credentials.
Periodic access review:
- Quarterly access reviews are required for all admin roles. Team leads must attest to the access list. Audit logs will be retained per the data retention schedule.
Emergency access procedure:
- Follow the Emergency Access Runbook (linked). Any manual bypass requires post-facto ticket and 1:1 review with Security within 48 hours.

2) Change Management (applies to infra, production services, and security-affecting changes)
Purpose: Reduce risk from configuration and code changes while maintaining deployment velocity.
Change categories:
- Standard: routine, low-risk changes pre-approved by the change board (e.g., configuration updates with automated tests).
- Normal: changes that require review and scheduled deployment window (e.g., new service rollout, infra scaling).
- Emergency: immediate fixes to stop production degradation or security incidents.
Process summary:
- All Normal changes require a Change Request (CR) via the Change Tracker and must include roll-back plan, risk assessment, and owner.
- Change review SLA: 72 hours for Normal changes; Standard changes require automated verification and are eligible for automated approval.
- Scheduled change windows: Weekdays 02:00-05:00 UTC for infra-impacting activities (exceptions require approval).
- Post-change verification: Owners must run the change checklist and publish verification results within 24 hours.
Change advisory board (CAB):
- Membership: Infra lead, SRE lead, Security, Product Ops (rotating).
- Weekly cadence: review Normal changes, policy updates, and retro on incidents linked to change activity.
Rollbacks and runbooks:
- Every Normal and Emergency change must include a rollback plan and playbook link. The SRE runbook directory holds standardized rollback steps.

3) Data Management
Purpose: Protect customer and company data through classification, handling, and retention policies.
Data classification levels:
- Public: Intended for external release (marketing collateral, public docs). No special controls.
- Internal: Company-internal documents (non-sensitive roadmaps, operational notes). Default for most docs.
- Confidential: Employee PII, vendor contracts, non-public financials. Access on a need-to-know basis.
- Restricted: Customer data, production logs containing PII or proprietary data, and regulated data. Requires explicit security approval for access.
Handling rules by classification:
- Encryption: All Confidential and Restricted data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Key management follows Security & Compliance guidelines.
- Storage: Restricted data should be stored only in approved locations (private buckets, VPC-only services).
- Transfer: Any transfer of Restricted data outside approved accounts or regions requires Security & Compliance sign-off and, if applicable, customer consent.
Retention & deletion:
- Default retention for Internal and Confidential documents is 7 years unless otherwise specified.
- Restricted data retention is determined by contractual terms; default is 3 years unless a longer term is required by contract/regulation.
- Data deletion requests follow the Data Subject Request (DSR) process; Security & Legal must be notified.
Data access request process:
1. Submit Data Access Request (DAR) with justification, dataset identifier, and intended use.
2. Security reviews and either approves, requests modifications, or rejects within 5 business days for routine requests. Expedited reviews are possible for operational emergencies.
Logging and audit:
- All access to Restricted datasets must have detailed audit logs. Logs are retained per the logging retention policy and accessible to Security for audits.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Purpose: Provide clear approval thresholds, preferred vendor lists, and expense reporting standards.
Procurement thresholds and approvals:
- <$1,000: Team lead approval.
- $1,000- $10,000: Team lead + Finance approval.
- $10,000- $50,000: Procurement team + Finance + Legal review for contractual terms.
- >$50,000: Executive sponsor + Procurement + Legal + Finance; procurement scope requires competitive bids unless sole-source justified.
Preferred vendor program:
- Finance maintains a preferred vendor list (cloud vendors, hardware partners, software licenses). Using preferred vendors shortens review times.
Purchase process:
1. Raise a Purchase Request in Procurement Portal with business justification and budget code.
2. Procurement reviews and issues PO, coordinates vendor contract (if applicable).
3. Vendor onboarding requires the Vendor Security Questionnaire (see Vendor Management section).
Expense policy summary:
- Employees must submit expense reports within 30 days. Late submissions require manager justification.
- Receipts required for all expenses > $25.
- Per diem and mileage: follow the published rates in the Travel Policy section.
- Corporate card use: follow the Cardholder Agreement; misuse will trigger review by Finance and People Ops.

5) Vendor Management
Purpose: Ensure consistent vendor risk assessment, onboarding, and contract lifecycle management.
Vendor onboarding checklist (required):
- Business justification and owner assigned.
- Vendor security questionnaire completed and reviewed by Security.
- Contract terms reviewed by Legal (data residency, confidentiality, SLAs).
- Procurement issues PO and records payment terms.
- Technical contacts and escalation contacts recorded in Vendor Directory.
Risk tiers & controls:
- Low risk: SaaS tools without access to customer or Restricted data (quarterly review).
- Medium risk: Services that process internal Confidential data or have limited access to production systems (security review + quarterly monitoring).
- High risk: Vendors that process Restricted/customer data or have privileged network access (annual SOC2/ISO attestation, encryption, contractual security commitments).
Contract renewals and terminations:
- Renewal notices must be raised 90 days prior to contract end.
- Termination procedure must include data return or secure deletion confirmation and verification by Security.

6) Travel Policy (business travel)
Purpose: Define allowable business travel expenses, approvals, and safety guidelines.
Booking and approvals:
- All travel must be pre-approved by the employee's manager and entered into the Travel Portal.
- Travel above $5,000 requires Finance pre-approval.
- Preferred booking channels are the company travel portal and preferred travel vendor partners.
Air travel:
- Economy for domestic flights under 5 hours. Premium economy or occasional upgrades require manager approval.
- Lowest reasonable fare that meets business constraints should be selected to reduce cost.
Lodging and per diem:
- Employees should select mid-range hotels on the preferred vendors list.
- Meal per diem is $60/day domestic, $80/day international (subject to local law).
Safety and incident reporting:
- Employees traveling for business must share itinerary with their manager and People Ops.
- Any incident (health, safety, security) during travel must be reported within 24 hours to People Ops and Security.
Expense reporting and reimbursement:
- Submit expense reports within 30 days with itemized receipts.
- Non-compliant expenses may be declined or reimbursed at company discretion.

7) Internal Templates and Forms (centralized links)
The following templates are maintained in the Templates directory and should be used as the canonical forms:
- Access Request Form (ARF) - use for access provisioning and temporary JIT escalation.
- Change Request Template (CR) - required for Normal changes.
- Data Access Request (DAR) - required for access to Restricted datasets.
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist & Security Questionnaire - required for new vendors.
- Purchase Request (PR) and PO template - used by Procurement.
- Expense Report template - for reimbursement submissions.
- Travel Itinerary & Risk Acknowledgement form - for international travel.
Templates are versioned and stored in the Templates folder (link) with owner metadata and last-reviewed dates.

Governance, reviews, and exceptions:
- Policy review cadence: This company-wide policy page is reviewed annually by People Ops, Finance, and Security.
- Emergency policy updates can be issued with an expedited review and retroactive CAB discussion.
- Exceptions: Temporary exceptions may be granted by the Policy Owner with documented justification and expiration date. All exceptions must be recorded in the Exceptions Log.

Audit, compliance, and reporting:
- Relevant metrics and artifacts (access review attestations, procurement logs, vendor security reviews) must be retained and made available for audits.
- Security will run annual vendor risk audits for high-risk vendors and spot checks for medium-risk vendors.
